votes.evidence:
I read the code at 1f24aba with git show. I did not create a worktree or run the CLI, and no checkout was changed. I checked the Unicode categories with node.

Code: hiddenChars (src/rules/injection.ts, around lines 78-92) flags only three things. Tag characters U+E0000-E007F and bidi controls U+202A-202E and U+2066-2069 are hard. Anything else matching /\p{Cf}/u is soft. escapeHidden (src/rules/util/text.ts:60-70) escapes only [\p{Cf}\p{Cc}]. No other guard exists. INJ-001 calls hiddenChars directly on corpus(snap) raw text, and snippet() routes through escapeHidden.

Category check with node: U+FE00, U+FE0F, U+E0100 and U+034F are Mn. U+115F, U+1160, U+3164 and U+FFA0 are Lo. U+2800 is So. None matches \p{Cf} and none matches \s. So hiddenChars returns nothing for them and escapeHidden leaves them raw.

NFKC: U+FE0x, U+E01xx, U+115F, U+1160, U+2800 and U+034F stay unchanged. U+3164 and U+FFA0 map to U+1160, which is still an invisible filler. So the claim "NFKC keeps all of them" is slightly loose, but the effect is the same. /ignore\s+previous/i on NFKC("Ignoreㅤpreviousㅤinstructions") returns false, so INJ-005-style regexes miss it.

This matches the spec. docs/design/spec.md:629-633 lists only tags, bidi controls and \p{Cf}. So this is a gap in the spec and its coverage, not a deviation from the spec. It is still a real evasion of a rule titled "Hidden or invisible characters". Byte smuggling with variation selectors U+E0100-E01EF after an emoji does the same job as tag characters, which are already flagged as error. I found nothing about these code points in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md. The only related item is the ZWJ/VS16 false positive at FINDINGS.md:1753, which is a different issue.

Severity: medium for the bypass. Under the project's principle, a fix should report these at warning level, or possibly hard for runs of U+E0100-E01EF. Variation selectors U+FE0E/U+FE0F that follow a pictograph must stay exempt.
